name: Action Point Economy
description: The per-turn budget: moving costs points, attacking costs points, items cost points, and when the wallet is empty the turn is over. combat.turn_order_queue says whose wallet is active; this component says what is inside it and what each action charges. Keeping the economy separate from the queue matters because games tune them independently — a boss with two turns is a queue change, a boss whose attacks cost double is an economy change, and neither should require touching the other's code. Unspent points never roll over by default: banking AP turns tactics into hoarding, so rollover is an explicit opt-in, not an accident.

implementations.note: Implemented in the consuming application; not verifiable from this repository.

inputs.name: actionPointsPerTurn
inputs.description: Base wallet size. Two is the genre's sweet spot: move-and-act, or act twice, but never everything.

inputs.name: actionCosts
inputs.description: Price list as data. Skills costing more than basics is what keeps the basic attack from becoming a typo.

inputs.name: allowPointBanking
inputs.description: Whether unspent points carry into the next turn. Opt-in only: banking rewards passing turns, which rewards boredom.

inputs.name: maxBankedPoints
inputs.description: Cap when banking is enabled. One banked point is a tactical reserve; three is a savings account.

outputs.name: pointsRemaining
outputs.description: Live wallet for the active unit.

outputs.name: actionsTaken
outputs.description: Actions spent this turn, for undo UI and replays.
